instructions:
You are reading the plain-language text of a codebase map. A reader meets each field ALONE, inside one box, with no paragraph around it, and does not read code.

Judge ONLY these two things:
  1. UNKNOWN WORD — a term the reader has not met and the field does not explain. Product words and words already in the map's Glossary are fine; jargon, an internal codename, or an unexplained abbreviation is not.
  2. LOST PRECISION — the sentence is short and plain but says nothing specific. "The system checks the user" is the shape: grammatical, readable, and it names no decision, no data and no actor. This is the worse failure, because it looks correct.

Do NOT report sentence length, em dashes, code names or an opening "It" — those are counted deterministically and the lead already has the numbers.
Be conservative. Report a field only when you can say WHICH word is unknown, or WHAT the sentence should have said. If in doubt, pass the field.

For each field you flag, return its `where` exactly as given, one of `unknown word` or `lost precision`, and one short line naming the word or the missing specific.

One tab in the viewer. Each answers a single question about the project.

The file and line a box points at. A box without one is ungrounded, which counts as a defect.
One goal one party has, with the thing that starts it and the result it ends in.
A group of use cases that serve one goal of the product.
One end to end run through the use cases that tells the product's story, with nothing going wrong.
The numbered steps of one use case. Each step says who or what acts, on what.
A run of steps that several flows all run. It is written once and referred to by each of them.
One place the product meets something that is not the product.
One address, command or tool an interface is made of.
One crossing between a person and the product, at an interface, inside one flow.
One module sized piece of the code, drawn as a single box.
A group of components, and of smaller subsystems under it.
One real named type the code defines, with its fields and its links to other types.
One decision the product makes, written in product words, plus every place it is enforced.
The report saying what a code change does to the map.
Folding a change impact report into the baseline and re-pinning it.
